text:
nightly-dashboard: [ALERT] p95 latency spike on /generate (model: redwood-small-2) in nightly run. p95 jumped from 48ms -> 220ms around 2026-11-21T02:14Z. Throughput down ~30%. link: https://dash.internal/redwood/runtime/nightly/2026-11-21

alice: saw that. is this correlated with the 02:14 deploy?

bryan: yeah deploy at 02:13:56, commit c3f4a9b. PR #4789 merged yesterday — it changed the kernel choice ordering for medium seq lengths.

carmen: PR #4789 swapped the selector to prefer fused-attn kernels first. I added a fallback path but maybe the ordering makes prefetch/handoff worse under certain batch shapes.

alice: can someone run the reproducer against that commit?

tim: running quick repro locally: ```./tools/perf_repro.sh --model redwood-small-2 --seq 512 --qps 80 --duration 60 --commit c3f4a9b```

nina: results from tim's run attached: p95=210ms, p50=32ms, cpu steal spikes around KV cache handoff logs. pasted extracted snippet:
```
[12:34:21] kernel_select: chosen=fused_attn_v2 fallback=stream_attn
[12:34:22] kv_cache: evict=128 -> miss_rate=0.12
[12:34:22] handoff: blocking on prefetch; waiting 12ms
[12:34:23] latency: sample p95=212ms
```

alice: that "blocking on prefetch" line is suspicious. we changed prefetch ordering in the same PR?

carmen: PR touched prefetch ordering heuristics to reduce wasted work at long seqs. but unit tests didn't cover mixed-batch shapes.

bryan: quick experiment: set RUNTIME_KERNEL_ORDER=legacy on a canary node and compare. if latency drops, we blame selector ordering.

tim: ran canary override with legacy ordering: ```export RUNTIME_KERNEL_ORDER=legacy && ./tools/perf_repro.sh --model redwood-small-2 --seq 512 --qps 80 --duration 60```

nina: canary with legacy: p95=54ms, p50=30ms, no handoff blocking logs. so seems strongly correlated.

alice: good repro. do we have a flamegraph / profile for the bad run?

bryan: uploaded perf traces and kernel traces: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/perf/1848123456/trace.zip. quick look shows long stalls in prefetch path and extra kernel context switches.

carmen: I'm preparing a minimal diff to revert the selector ordering change. will open PR to revert #4789 and re-run nightly.

ops-oncall: heads up, canary traffic already showing errors for customers on Dedicated. this should be prioritized for rollout-blocker.

alice: agreed. if revert fixes canary, let's fast-track. tim can you confirm revert locally?

tim: checked: revert PR #4795 created from branch revert/selector-4789. local run with revert: p95=50ms, throughput back to baseline.

deploy-bot: Revert PR #4795 created and linked: https://git.internal/redwood/repo/pulls/4795. Auto CI perf check queued.

bryan: CI perf check failed earlier for the original merge (it was marginal). looks like our perf guard didn't catch this shape. filing a follow-up to add mixed-batch e2e shape.

alice: next steps: 1) merge revert PR #4795 after approvals 2) add mixed-batch perf test to nightly harness (seqs 32/512 mixed) 3) add an integration test that sets prefetch ordering matrix 4) postmortem w/ root cause and lessons. owner: carmen for the revert + test, bryan for perf harness update.

carmen: ack, I'll shepherd revert and add the test. estimate 2-3 hours to get revert merged and canary redeployed.

nina: I'll run extended regressions once revert is live and confirm KV miss/hand-off metrics are stable.

ops-oncall: tagging sev:medium and creating internal incident ticket: INC-2026-1121.

alice: thanks everyone. please add any stray logs to the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
